metinler.baslik: Landing at Samsun: The General Situation
metinler.ne: Nutuk's famous first sentence and the state of the country in the spring of 1919.

satirlar.o: 1335 senesi Mayıs'ının on dokuzuncu günü Samsun'a çıktım.
satirlar.s: I landed at Samsun on 19 May 1919. (1335 is 1919 in the Rumi calendar used at the time.)

satirlar.o: Vaziyet ve manzara-i umumiye:
satirlar.s: This was the general situation and outlook:

satirlar.o: Osmanlı Devleti'nin dahil bulunduğu grup, Harb-i Umumi'de mağlup olmuş,
satirlar.s: The alliance the Ottoman State belonged to had been defeated in the First World War,

satirlar.o: Osmanlı ordusu her tarafta zedelenmiş, şeraiti ağır bir mütarekename imzalanmış.
satirlar.s: the army was worn down on every front, and a harsh armistice had been signed.

satirlar.o: Büyük Harbin uzun seneleri zarfında, millet yorgun ve fakir bir halde.
satirlar.s: After long years of war the nation was exhausted and poor.

satirlar.o: Millet ve memleketi Harb-i Umumi'ye sevk edenler, kendi hayatları endişesine düşerek memleketten firar etmişler.
satirlar.s: Those who had dragged the nation into the war had fled the country to save their own skins.

satirlar.o: Ordunun elinden esliha ve cephanesi alınmış ve alınmakta.
satirlar.s: The army had been stripped of its weapons and ammunition, and still was being stripped.

satirlar.a: Four days earlier, on 15 May, the Greek army had landed at İzmir. The French were at Adana, the British on the Antep–Maraş–Urfa line, the Italians at Antalya and Konya.

metinler.ne: The decision for full independence against the talk of mandates and protection.

satirlar.a: At the time three ways of deliverance were being put forward.
The first was to ask for British protection, the second to accept an American mandate.
The third was for each region to fend for itself.
Mustafa Kemal accepted none of them: all of them gave up the nation's independence.

satirlar.o: Efendiler, bu vaziyet karşısında bir tek karar vardı.
satirlar.s: Gentlemen, in these circumstances there was only one decision.

satirlar.o: O da hâkimiyet-i milliyeye müstenid, bilâkayd ü şart müstakil yeni bir Türk Devleti tesis etmek!
satirlar.s: It was to found a new Turkish State, based on national sovereignty and unconditionally independent!

satirlar.a: According to Nutuk this decision was made before leaving Istanbul and put into practice the moment he set foot on Anatolian soil at Samsun.

metinler.baslik: The Amasya Circular: The Nation's Resolve Will Save Its Independence
metinler.ne: The first document to state together the aim, the reason and the method of the National Struggle.

satirlar.a: After rousing the people with meetings at Havza, Mustafa Kemal met his comrades-in-arms at Amasya.

satirlar.o: Vatanın tamamiyeti, milletin istiklali tehlikededir.
satirlar.s: The integrity of the country and the independence of the nation are in danger.

satirlar.o: Hükümet-i merkeziye deruhde ettiği mes'ûliyetin icâbâtını ifa edememektedir.
satirlar.s: The Istanbul government cannot carry out the responsibility it has taken on.

satirlar.o: Milletin istiklalini yine milletin azim ve kararı kurtaracaktır.
satirlar.s: The nation's own resolve and determination will save the nation's independence.

satirlar.a: It was decided that a national congress representing the whole country should meet at Sivas.
The circular was signed by Mustafa Kemal with Rauf, Ali Fuat and Refet; Kâzım Karabekir joined by telegraph.

metinler.baslik: Resigning from the Army: As One of the Nation
metinler.ne: The decision to lay down every official title and carry on the struggle as a civilian.

satirlar.a: The Istanbul government had dismissed Mustafa Kemal and ordered him to return at once.
On the night of 8 July 1919 he sat down at the telegraph in Erzurum.
He announced that he was resigning both his official post and the army.
He no longer had rank or office; he would carry on the struggle as one of the nation.
He gave up the profession he loved most, soldiering, for the cause.
Kâzım Karabekir, commander of the XVth Corps, did not arrest him; on the contrary, he declared himself at his orders.

metinler.baslik: The Erzurum Congress: The Homeland Is One Whole
metinler.ne: The first congress that met regionally but decided for the whole homeland.

satirlar.a: On 23 July 1919 delegates of the eastern provinces met at Erzurum.
Mustafa Kemal was elected chairman of the congress.
Resolution: within the national frontiers the homeland is one whole and cannot be divided.
The nation will resist together every foreign occupation and interference.
If the Istanbul government cannot protect the homeland, a provisional government will be formed.
Mandates and protection are unacceptable.

satirlar.o: Kuvâ-yı milliyeyi âmil ve irâde-i milliyeyi hâkim kılmak esastır.
satirlar.s: The principle is to make the national forces the driving power and the national will sovereign.

satirlar.a: The congress closed on 7 August; Mustafa Kemal headed the Representative Committee it elected.

metinler.baslik: The Sivas Congress: All Societies Under One Roof
metinler.ne: Here the organisation of the National Struggle covering the whole country was founded.

satirlar.a: On 4 September 1919 delegates from every part of Anatolia and Rumelia met at Sivas.
All the national societies were united under the name 'Society for the Defence of the Rights of Anatolia and Rumelia'.
The principle laid down at Erzurum was repeated here for the whole country: the national forces would be the driving power and the national will sovereign.
The idea of a mandate or protection was rejected for good.
The Istanbul government's attempts to break up the congress came to nothing; Anatolia cut its telegraph links with Istanbul.
At the beginning of October the Damat Ferit government fell. Anatolia now spoke with one voice.

metinler.baslik: Arrival in Ankara: The Heart of the Struggle
metinler.ne: The Representative Committee's choice of Ankara as its centre.

satirlar.a: The Representative Committee arrived in Ankara on 27 December 1919.
Ankara was on the railway, close enough to Istanbul and far enough from the front.
The people, the seymen and the efe welcomed the Committee with joy.
A small Anatolian town would become the capital of the new state within a few years.

metinler.baslik: The National Pact and the Occupation of Istanbul
metinler.ne: The declaration of the national frontiers and Ankara's answer to the occupation of Istanbul.

satirlar.a: The last Ottoman Chamber of Deputies adopted the National Pact on 28 January 1920.
Under it, the lands held when the armistice was signed and inhabited mostly by Turks were one indivisible whole.
The Allies answered by formally occupying Istanbul on 16 March 1920.
The Chamber was raided; some deputies were arrested and exiled to Malta.
Mustafa Kemal acted the same day: an assembly with extraordinary powers would meet in Ankara.

metinler.baslik: 23 April 1920: The Grand National Assembly Opens
metinler.ne: The birth of a new assembly founded on national sovereignty.

satirlar.a: On Friday 23 April 1920 the Grand National Assembly of Turkey opened in Ankara.
In the nation's name the Assembly took both legislative and executive power into its own hands.
Mustafa Kemal was elected President of the Assembly.
The first article of the first constitution, adopted in January 1921, wrote down the principle:

satirlar.o: Hâkimiyet bilâkaydüşart milletindir.
satirlar.s: Sovereignty belongs to the nation without condition.

metinler.baslik: İnönü: You Have Also Defeated the Nation's Ill Fate
metinler.ne: The regular army's first victories and a telegram that went down in history.

satirlar.a: The regular army passed its first test on the Western Front, at İnönü, under İsmet Pasha.
The First Battle of İnönü in January 1921 raised the Assembly's standing.
At the end of March the Greek army attacked again; the Second Battle of İnönü was won on 31 March 1921.
Mustafa Kemal watched the battlefield from Metristepe and sent İsmet Pasha this telegram:

satirlar.o: Siz orada yalnız düşmanı değil, milletin makûs talihini de yendiniz.
satirlar.s: There you have defeated not only the enemy but also the nation's ill fate.

metinler.baslik: Sakarya: There Is No Line of Defence, There Is a Plain of Defence
metinler.ne: The turning point of the war and the order to defend the 'plain'.

satirlar.a: After the defeat at Kütahya–Eskişehir the army fell back east of the Sakarya River.
On 5 August 1921 the Assembly gave Mustafa Kemal the powers of Commander-in-Chief for three months.
Under the National Requisition orders the people gave part of what they had to the army: socks, sandals, wheat, horses, ox-carts.

satirlar.o: Hatt-ı müdafaa yoktur, sath-ı müdafaa vardır. O satıh bütün vatandır.
satirlar.s: There is no line to defend, there is a plain to defend. That plain is the whole homeland.

satirlar.o: Vatanın her karış toprağı, vatandaşın kanıyla ıslanmadıkça terk olunamaz.
satirlar.s: Not an inch of the homeland may be given up until it is soaked in the blood of its citizens.

satirlar.a: The battle lasted 22 days and 22 nights and ended in victory on 13 September 1921.
The Assembly gave Mustafa Kemal the rank of Marshal and the title of Gazi.

metinler.baslik: Armies! Your First Goal Is the Mediterranean
metinler.ne: The last and decisive victory of the War of Independence.

satirlar.a: On the morning of 26 August 1922 the Great Offensive began from Kocatepe.
On 30 August the Commander-in-Chief's Battle was won at Dumlupınar.
On 1 September the Commander-in-Chief gave the army this order:

satirlar.o: Ordular! İlk hedefiniz Akdeniz'dir. İleri!

satirlar.a: On 9 September 1922 Turkish cavalry entered İzmir.
On 11 October the Armistice of Mudanya was signed; Eastern Thrace was recovered without a fight.

metinler.ne: The end of a six-century sultanate.

satirlar.a: The invitation of both Ankara and Istanbul to the peace talks showed it was time to end the double rule.
When the debate in the Assembly committee dragged on, Mustafa Kemal took the floor:

satirlar.o: Hâkimiyet ve saltanat hiç kimse tarafından hiç kimseye, ilim icabıdır diye, müzakere ile, münakaşa ile verilmez.
satirlar.s: Sovereignty and sultanate are not given to anyone by debate and discussion because scholarship requires it.

satirlar.o: Hâkimiyet, saltanat, kuvvetle, kudretle ve zorla alınır.
satirlar.s: Sovereignty and sultanate are taken by strength, by power and by force.

satirlar.a: The sultanate was abolished on 1 November 1922.
The last sultan, Vahdettin, left the country on a British warship on 17 November.

metinler.baslik: Lausanne: The New Turkey at the Table
metinler.ne: The War of Independence's victory at the table.

satirlar.a: The delegation led by İsmet Pasha negotiated at Lausanne for months.
The talks broke down in February 1923 and resumed in April.
The treaty signed on 24 July 1923 introduced the new Turkish state to the world.
The centuries-old capitulations were abolished.
Some questions, such as Mosul and the Straits, were left for later; the Straits came under full Turkish control with the Montreux Convention of 1936.

metinler.baslik: Tomorrow We Shall Proclaim the Republic!
metinler.ne: The night the Republic was proclaimed.

satirlar.a: In October 1923 there was a government crisis; no cabinet could be formed.
At dinner at Çankaya on the evening of 28 October, Mustafa Kemal told his friends:

satirlar.o: Yarın Cumhuriyet ilân edeceğiz!
satirlar.s: Tomorrow we shall proclaim the Republic!

satirlar.a: On the evening of 29 October 1923 the Assembly amended the constitution and proclaimed the Republic.
That same night Mustafa Kemal was unanimously elected the first President; İsmet Pasha became Prime Minister.
A 101-gun salute was fired in Ankara.

metinler.ne: A great step towards a unified education and a secular state.

satirlar.a: On 3 March 1924 the Assembly passed three important laws on the same day.
The Caliphate was abolished; the Ottoman dynasty was sent abroad.
With the Law on the Unification of Education, all schools were brought under one roof, the Ministry of Education.
The Ministry of Religious Law and Foundations was abolished; the Presidency of Religious Affairs was set up in its place.
On 20 April of the same year the new constitution was adopted.

metinler.baslik: Six Days, Thirty-Six and a Half Hours: Nutuk Is Read

satirlar.a: On 15 October 1927 the Second Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party met in Ankara.
The Gazi took the rostrum and spoke for six days, close to thirty-six and a half hours in all.
He told everything that happened from 1919 to 1927 one by one, with documents, telegrams and orders.
Most of his listeners had witnessed the events; the speech was prepared like an accounting.
On 20 October 1927 he spoke his last words to the Turkish youth.
Nutuk was printed the same year in Arabic letters, together with a volume of documents.

metinler.ne: The last words of Nutuk: the Republic entrusted to the youth.

satirlar.o: Ey Türk gençliği! Birinci vazifen, Türk istiklalini, Türk Cumhuriyetini, ilelebet muhafaza ve müdafaa etmektir.
satirlar.s: O Turkish Youth! Your first duty is to preserve and defend Turkish independence and the Turkish Republic for ever.

satirlar.o: Mevcudiyetinin ve istikbalinin yegâne temeli budur. Bu temel, senin en kıymetli hazinendir.
satirlar.s: This is the only basis of your existence and your future. This basis is your most precious treasure.

satirlar.o: İstikbalde dahi, seni bu hazineden mahrum etmek isteyecek dahilî ve haricî bedhahların olacaktır.
satirlar.s: In the future, too, there will be ill-wishers at home and abroad who want to deprive you of this treasure.

satirlar.o: Bir gün, istiklal ve cumhuriyeti müdafaa mecburiyetine düşersen, vazifeye atılmak için, içinde bulunacağın vaziyetin imkân ve şeraitini düşünmeyeceksin!
satirlar.s: If one day you are compelled to defend your independence and the Republic, you will not stop to weigh the possibilities and conditions of the situation you are in before taking up your duty!

satirlar.o: Bu imkân ve şerait, çok namüsait bir mahiyette tezahür edebilir.
satirlar.s: These possibilities and conditions may be extremely unfavourable.

satirlar.o: İstiklal ve cumhuriyetine kastedecek düşmanlar, bütün dünyada emsali görülmemiş bir galibiyetin mümessili olabilirler.
satirlar.s: The enemies plotting against your independence and your Republic may be the representatives of a victory unseen in the world.

satirlar.o: Cebren ve hile ile aziz vatanın bütün kaleleri zapt edilmiş, bütün tersanelerine girilmiş, bütün orduları dağıtılmış ve memleketin her köşesi bilfiil işgal edilmiş olabilir.
satirlar.s: By force and by trickery, all the fortresses of your beloved homeland may have been captured, all its shipyards entered, all its armies dispersed and every corner of the country actually occupied.

satirlar.o: Bütün bu şeraitten daha elîm ve daha vahim olmak üzere, memleketin dahilinde iktidara sahip olanlar gaflet ve dalalet ve hatta hıyanet içinde bulunabilirler.
satirlar.s: More bitter and more dangerous than all this, those who hold power within the country may be in error, misguided, even traitors.

satirlar.o: Hatta bu iktidar sahipleri şahsi menfaatlerini, müstevlilerin siyasi emelleriyle tevhid edebilirler.
satirlar.s: These rulers may even join their personal interests to the political aims of the invaders.

satirlar.o: Millet, fakr u zaruret içinde harap ve bitap düşmüş olabilir.
satirlar.s: The nation may be ruined and exhausted by poverty and hardship.

satirlar.o: Ey Türk istikbalinin evladı! İşte, bu ahval ve şerait içinde dahi vazifen, Türk istiklal ve cumhuriyetini kurtarmaktır!
satirlar.s: O child of Turkey's future! Even in these circumstances and conditions, your duty is to save Turkish independence and the Republic!

satirlar.o: Muhtaç olduğun kudret, damarlarındaki asil kanda mevcuttur!
satirlar.s: The strength you need is in the noble blood in your veins!

biliyormu: 🎙️ Nutuk was read over 6 days, 15–20 October 1927, in about 36.5 hours
🚢 The steamer Bandırma left Istanbul for Samsun on 16 May 1919
📐 The book 'Geometry' was printed in 1937 without an author's name; its author was Atatürk
✍️ The surname 'Atatürk' was given on 24 November 1934 by a special law of the Assembly
⏳ The Battle of the Sakarya lasted 22 days and 22 nights
🎼 Mehmet Akif refused the prize money of the Independence March competition
🗳️ On the night the Republic was proclaimed, 158 deputies elected Mustafa Kemal unanimously
🔤 Adults learned the new letters in the Nation's Schools, opened on 1 January 1929
🎖️ There is no regiment numbered 57 in the Turkish army: in memory of Gallipoli
🏛️ Ankara became the capital on 13 October 1923, two weeks before the Republic
👩 Women won the vote in municipal elections in 1930, village elections in 1933 and parliamentary elections in 1934
🕰️ The international clock and calendar came into use on 1 January 1926
📏 The Measures Law of 1931 brought in the metre and the kilogram
📅 The weekly holiday moved from Friday to Sunday in 1935
👋 In 1934 titles such as 'efendi, bey, pasha' were abolished; 'Bay' and 'Bayan' (Mr and Mrs) took their place
🔬 'The truest guide in life is science' is written on the front of the Faculty of Language, History and Geography in Ankara
📡 The National Struggle was largely run by telegraph; Nutuk is full of telegrams
📚 By Atatürk's will, the income of his İş Bankası shares went to the Turkish Historical and Language societies
